financialInsti.name: PhilHealth
financialInsti.description: PhilHealth is the Philippines' government-owned health insurer, providing universal health coverage through a social insurance program. It pools funds from member contributions to subsidize medical costs, making healthcare affordable for hospitalizations and preventive care.

programs.programDescription: Government program that helps Filipinos take care of their health and prevent illness. YAKAP Clinics watch over members' health, find illness early, and give the right medicines so the illness does not get worse and hospital stays are avoided.

benefits.benefitName: Primary Care Checkup

Selected laboratory tests based on risk, age and health assessment: Complete Blood Count (CBC) with Platelet Count, Lipid Profile, Fasting Blood Sugar (FBS), Oral Glucose Tolerance Test (OGTT), Hemoglobin Test (HbA1c), Creatinine, Chest X-Ray, Sputum Microscopy, Electrocardiogram (ECG), Urinalysis, Pap Smear, Fecalysis, Fecal Occult Blood Test (FOBT), Upper Abdomen & Pelvic Ultrasound
Medicines under PhilHealth GAMOT
Breast cancer screening: Breast Ultrasound & Mammogram
Liver cancer screening: Alpha Fetoprotein Test & Liver Ultrasound
Colorectal cancer screening: Fecal Immunochemical Test, Fecal Occult Blood Test & Colonoscopy
Lung cancer screening: Low-dose Chest CT Scan

requirements.requirementDescription: PhilHealth Identification Number (PIN) with updated membership

procedure.instruction: Register: make sure you have a PhilHealth Identification Number (PIN) and your membership is updated.
Choose a YAKAP Clinic using the eGovPH Super App, the PhilHealth Member Portal, or the nearest PhilHealth office.
Have your First Patient Encounter (FPE): medical history, health screening and health education.
Sign the form agreeing that your chosen YAKAP Clinic will keep caring for you.
Keep seeing your YAKAP doctor for prescriptions, referrals for laboratory and/or cancer screening tests when needed, and follow-up checkups.

programs.programDescription:
PhilHealth's Z Benefits packages for selected cancers, at Z Benefits contracted health facilities. Each cancer has its own package and medical criteria; the hospital's Z Benefits coordinator checks them.

Breast Cancer (cStage 0 to IV): PhilHealth's Z Benefit package for breast cancer, up to P1.4 million (effective March 30, 2024). It covers diagnostic tests, surgery, hormonotherapy, chemotherapy, targeted therapy and surveillance after surgery, at Z Benefits contracted health facilities. Up to five (5) days are deducted from the 45-day annual benefit limit.

Acute Lymphocytic / Lymphoblastic Leukemia (standard risk): PhilHealth's Z Benefit package for children with standard-risk acute lymphoblastic leukemia: five hundred thousand pesos (Php 500,000) for the complete course of treatment for three (3) years, paid to the contracted health facility in three tranches. Pre-authorization must be submitted before the end of the induction phase.

Prostate Cancer (low to intermediate risk): PhilHealth's Z Benefit package for localized low- to intermediate-risk prostate cancer, at Z Benefits contracted health facilities.

Cervical Cancer: PhilHealth's Z Benefit package for cervical cancer treatment (chemoradiation with brachytherapy, or primary surgery for early stages), at Z Benefits contracted health facilities.

Colorectal Cancer: PhilHealth's Z Benefit package for colon and rectal cancer. The amount depends on the cancer, its stage and risk. Available at Z Benefits contracted health facilities. Up to five (5) days are deducted from the 45-day annual benefit limit.

financialInsti.name: Philippine Charity Sweepstakes Office (PCSO)
financialInsti.description: Government agency that gives financial help to people with health problems through its Medical Assistance Program, together with government and private hospitals, health facilities and medicine retailers.

branches.location: Maharlika Center, J.P Cabagui Avenue, Davao City

eligibility: Individuals with health-related problems seeking financial help
programs.programDescription: Financial help for patients, given in partnership with government and private hospitals, health facilities, medicine retailers and other partners. Cancer treatment (chemotherapy drugs, immunotherapy and radiation therapy) is one of the types of help. If approved, the patient gets a Guarantee Letter (GL) for the hospital, health facility, medicine retailer or diagnostic center.

benefits.benefitName: Cancer treatment: chemotherapeutic drugs and immunotherapy
Radiation therapy
Confinement assistance
Laboratory, diagnostic and imaging procedures (such as CT-Scan, MRI, PET Scan and biopsy)

requirements.requirementDescription: Valid proof of identity of the patient (government-issued ID or other accepted ID)
Valid ID of the patient's next of kin, if applicable

For cancer treatment: updated clinical or medical abstract (issued within the past 3 months), medical prescription, and treatment protocol (chemotherapy) or treatment plan (radiation therapy), each with the full name, signature and license number of the attending physician
For cancer treatment: one quotation from the hospital willing to accept the GL, or official quotations from three different suppliers if the medicine is not available in the hospital

procedure.instruction: Apply online through the Online MAP Application (steps 2 to 6), or go to the PCSO Davao City Branch, or to the PCSO or Malasakit Center desk of your hospital. In some areas, MAP can be accessed only through hospitals with a Malasakit Center.
Go to www.pcso.gov.ph, select "E-Services", then "Online MAP Application", and create an account.
Log in with your name, date of birth and email, and enter the one-time code sent to your email.
Click "Apply Now", choose the partner health facility, its city and the type of request, then get a queuing number.
Upload all required documents as PDF files (not more than 2MB each) and submit the application.
Wait for the result in your email or in your online account.

financialInsti.name: Department of Health (DOH)
financialInsti.description: National government department for health. Its MAIFIP program helps pay the medical bills of patients who cannot afford them, and its Cancer Assistance Fund (CAF) and CSPMAP help cancer patients with treatment and free medicines.

branches.location: PRRD Bldg Bajada, Davao City (infront SPMC Hospital)
Malasakit Center, Bajada, Davao City (beside SPMC Hospital)

programs.programName: Medical Assistance for Indigent and Financially Incapacitated Patients (MAIFIP)
eligibility: Indigent and financially incapacitated patients who cannot afford their medical expenses
Including PhilHealth members whose remaining bill is still too big
programs.programDescription: Covers the remaining out-of-pocket hospital bill after PhilHealth and other discounts.

benefits.benefitName: Remaining medical bill after PhilHealth and other discounts

requirements.requirementDescription: In-patients: Hospital bill or charges or fees or statement of account (SOA)

In-patients: Copy of valid ID of the patient or medical social services-issued ID or barangay-issued Certificate of Residence (for GIDA areas) or Certification from Indigenous People (IP) representatives (for IPs) or valid ID of next of kin, if applicable.
Out-patients: Prescription of drugs and medicines or treatment protocol or laboratory or diagnostic request issued by referring facilities, if applicable.

Out-patients: Copy of valid ID of the patient or medical social services-issued ID or barangay-issued Certificate of Residence (for GIDA areas) or Certification from Indigenous People (IP) representatives (for IPs) or valid ID of next of kin, if applicable.

procedure.instruction: Get a consultation or treatment at a hospital that has a Malasakit Center.
Go to the Malasakit Center office inside the hospital for your medical or financial needs.
Have an interview and assessment with the assigned social worker.
Submit the required documents to receive the benefits.
Receive the approved medical or financial benefit.

eligibility: Persons with cancer, cancer survivors and high-risk individuals
For the eight priority cancer types
programs.programDescription: DOH fund under RA 11215 (National Integrated Cancer Control Act). It pays for cancer prevention, screening, early detection and diagnosis, treatment and care-related components for 8 priority cancer types. It adds to PhilHealth and other help for costs they do not cover, and for cancer cases it is used before MAIP. In Davao City, Southern Philippines Medical Center is a CAF access site (one of 34 in DOH's 2025 list).
cancerTypes: Liver cancer, including colorectal and other digestive tract cancers
Head and neck cancers, including thyroid
Prostate, renal and urinary bladder cancer

benefits.benefitName: Diagnostic procedures, medicines and treatment

requirements.requirementDescription: Medical abstract, doctor's prescription, or treatment plan

procedure.instruction: Go to a CAF access site. In Davao City: Southern Philippines Medical Center.
Present your medical abstract, doctor's prescription, or treatment plan to the social worker assigned to the hospital for assessment and approval.
Your documents are evaluated before approval and availment of services.

programs.programName: Cancer and Supportive-Palliative Medicines Access Program (CSPMAP)
programs.programDescription: DOH program that gives free medicines not yet covered by PhilHealth, to lower or remove out-of-pocket costs. It is part of the National Integrated Cancer Control Program. Its DOH hospital access sites are also CAF access sites. In 2024, 35 access sites offered 61 medicines for the most common cancers.

benefits.benefitName: Free medicines not yet covered by PhilHealth
